W1.name: Ines Okafor
W1.text: Ines Okafor arrived on Harrow Quay as the new keeper of the Salt Ledger, the only passenger on the ferry.
W1.quote: Ines Okafor was its only passenger

W2.name: Tobiah Wren
W2.text: Tobiah Wren was the old ferryman who steered with his right hand and carried Ines Okafor to Harrow Quay.
W2.quote: The ferryman was an old man named Tobiah Wren

W3.name: Aldous Brandt
W3.text: Aldous Brandt was the former keeper of the Salt Ledger for thirty years, and he had been gone for three weeks.
W3.quote: He kept that book for thirty years.

G1.text: Ines Okafor was sent to take up the post of Keeper of the Salt Ledger on Harrow Quay.

E1.text: Tobiah Wren said he did not carry Aldous Brandt off the island, contradicting the printed account that Brandt had simply left.

E2.text: Tobiah Wren gave Ines Okafor a small brass key that Aldous Brandt had given him, and told her to keep it off the ledger.
E2.quote: he took something from his pocket and pressed it into her glove

E3.text: Tobiah Wren left Ines Okafor on the quay and sailed north to the cod banks, not returning before the equinox.
E3.quote: would not return before the equinox

Q1.text: It is unknown what the brass key that Ines Okafor received from Tobiah Wren opens.
Q1.quote: He did not say, and I did not ask

Q2.text: It is unknown how Aldous Brandt left Harrow Quay if he was not carried by ferry.

W4.name: Mara Venn
W4.text: Mara Venn is the harbourmaster, who led Ines Okafor to the archive and asked for the Salt Ledger audit to be finished.
W4.quote: The council needs the audit finished before the equinox market,

W5.name: Anselm Pike
W5.text: Anselm Pike is the island's physician and printer, who brought Ines Okafor supper and offered to help with the book.
W5.quote: I am the physician here, and also the printer, since nobody else has a press.

W6.name: The Crane Company
W6.text: The Crane Company is an outside firm that has offered to buy the island's fishing rights.
W6.quote: The Crane Company has offered to buy the island's fishing rights.

G2.text: Ines Okafor was asked by the council, through Mara Venn, to finish the audit of the Salt Ledger before the equinox market.
G2.quote: The council needs the audit finished before the equinox market,

E4.text: Ines Okafor found the spring pages of the Salt Ledger torn out, and Mara Venn said the book was found that way the morning Brandt was gone.
E4.quote: We found the book like that the morning Brandt was gone.

E5.text: Anselm Pike brought Ines Okafor soup and told her he had played chess with Aldous Brandt every Thursday for eleven years.
E5.quote: told her that he had played chess with Aldous Brandt every Thursday for eleven years

E6.text: Ines Okafor noticed a locked brass tide-clock set into the wall on the landing below the archive.
E6.quote: its brass case locked and its single hand pointing at high water.

Q3.text: It is unknown whether Aldous Brandt took the torn spring pages with him, as some people claim.
Q3.quote: Some say he took them with him.

Q4.text: It is unknown what Mara Venn knows about Aldous Brandt's disappearance, since she says she knows nothing.
Q4.quote: I say only what I know, and I know nothing.

W7.name: Mara Lisle
W7.text: Mara Lisle is a girl of about nineteen who mends trawls in the net loft and has run errands for Aldous Brandt since she was twelve.
W7.quote: Mara Lisle had run Brandt's errands since she was twelve.

W8.name: The Cormorant
W8.text: The Cormorant is the unnamed writer of a note, marked with an ink seabird, that was pushed under the archive door.
W8.quote: In place of a signature someone had drawn a small black seabird in ink.

G3.text: Ines Okafor set out in the morning to find anyone who had worked with Aldous Brandt.
G3.quote: Ines went looking for anyone who had worked with Brandt

E7.text: Mara Lisle said that in his last month Aldous Brandt stopped sleeping, went to the salt warehouse at night, and returned with chalk on his sleeves.
E7.quote: He went down to the salt warehouse at night with a lantern

E8.text: An unsigned note was pushed under the archive door, saying the spring pages were not burned, and Ines Okafor locked it in her trunk.
E8.quote: "The spring pages are not burned," the note said.

Q5.text: It is unknown what Aldous Brandt was counting in the salt warehouse, and why he never told Mara Lisle.

Q6.text: It is unknown whether the spring pages are truly unburned, as the Cormorant's note claims.
Q6.quote: "The spring pages are not burned," the note said.

G4.text: Ines Okafor asked Mara Venn to open the sealed salt warehouse so that she could count its barrels.
G4.quote: she asked the harbourmaster to open the salt warehouse

E9.text: Ines Okafor counted salt over four days and found that 24 barrels a month arrived on the island without reaching the ledger.
E9.quote: Twenty-four barrels a month had come onto the island

E10.text: Mara Venn refused to open the salt warehouse without a council order, saying it was sealed until the market.
E10.quote: The warehouse is sealed until the market.

E11.text: That night a second note signed by the Cormorant was pushed under the archive door.
E11.quote: there was a second note under the door

Q7.text: It is unknown whether Mara Venn is the person Ines Okafor is looking for, since Ines Okafor only wondered it after being refused.
Q7.quote: she wondered whether the woman who held the seal

Q8.text: It is unknown who writes the tide tables, which the Cormorant's second note asks Ines Okafor to find out.
Q8.quote: Ask who writes the tide tables.

G5.text: Ines Okafor planned to carry her salt tally to the council in the morning.
G5.quote: She meant to carry this tally to the council in the morning.

E12.text: Ines Okafor copied her salt count onto one sheet, showing forty barrels in the book against sixty-four on the receipts, month by month.
E12.quote: forty barrels in the book, sixty-four on the receipts

E13.text: Someone climbed the tower stairs just before midnight, passed the landing, and entered the archive after the lamp went out.
E13.quote: they did not stop at the landing

E14.text: The unseen visitor took Ines Okafor's salt tally from the desk, while the ledger and the biscuit tin of receipts were left untouched.
E14.quote: The tally was gone from the desk.

Q9.text: It is unknown who stood beside Ines Okafor in the dark, or why they took only her salt tally sheet.
Q9.quote: She did not know who had stood beside her in the dark

Q10.text: It is unknown how the archive lamp went out, since Ines Okafor says she had not touched it.

G6.text: Ines Okafor was asked by Anselm Pike to bring the biscuit tin of receipts to his dispensary strongbox that night.

E15.text: Ines Okafor realised the printed tide table was wrong, since the harbour had been high at midnight and a boat could land only then.
E15.quote: the water had been high against the quay

E16.text: Ines Okafor kept the biscuit tin of receipts under her coat and did not take it to Anselm Pike's dispensary.
E16.quote: did not take it to the dispensary.

E17.text: Anselm Pike said that Mara Venn's coat smelled of tar and juniper, and offered to keep the receipts in his strongbox.

Q11.text: It is unknown whether the midnight visitor who took the salt tally came by boat at high water.
Q11.quote: A boat could land on the outer steps only at high water

Q12.text: Anselm Pike hinted at Mara Venn's coat, but it is not stated whether she entered the archive or took the salt tally.
Q12.quote: But you have met our harbourmaster's coat.

W9.name: Mara Lisle
W9.text: Mara Lisle is the Cormorant, the writer of the unsigned notes, who watched boats come in at night and wrote to the keeper.

W10.name: Anselm Pike
W10.text: Anselm Pike is named beside the Crane Company in Brandt's spring pages, and Ines concludes that he sold salt off the book.
W10.quote: The doctor had been curing fish off the book

E18.text: Mara Lisle showed Ines Okafor an ink seabird and said she had drawn it as the Cormorant.
E18.quote: I drew the bird," she said.

E19.text: Ines Okafor and Mara Lisle used the brass key on the tide-clock case and found the missing spring pages rolled behind its hand.
E19.quote: Behind the single hand, rolled tight and tied with twine

E20.text: The spring pages show twenty-four barrels of salt a month sent to the outer steps, each entry marked with the names A. Pike and the Crane Company.
E20.quote: against each entry the same two names

Q13.text: It is unknown whether Aldous Brandt left the island or was harmed after he found the spring pages.

Q14.text: It is unknown whether the Crane Company knew that the salt was being sold off the book.

W11.name: Mara Venn
W11.text: Mara Venn, the harbourmaster, not Mara Lisle, took Ines Okafor's salt tally from the archive and locked it in the council chest.

E21.text: Aldous Brandt escaped Pike's men in a skiff and was hidden by Tobiah Wren for three weeks, then returned on the equinox ferry.
E21.quote: When Pike's men came for him he had got away in a skiff

E22.text: Anselm Pike was taken at his press, with the next month's false tide tables still wet on the rack.
E22.quote: Dr Pike was taken at his press

E23.text: The council refused the Crane Company's offer for the fishing rights, and its agent left on the afternoon ferry.
E23.quote: The Crane Company's offer was refused, and its agent left

units.title: 7. The Door That Isn't a Door
